name: review-budget-stall-adjudication
title: Turn the advisory review-convergence stall detector into a mandatory blocking adjudication so a story cannot mint unlimited ordinary review rounds without a recorded escalation, re-plan, finding resolution, or unreachable-item declaration
description:
Step 3 of the evidence-integrity program (docs/evidence-integrity-program-spec.md §3): the review-budget circuit breaker. Today a story's review can balloon to 20+ rounds with no effective brake — the S3 incident and the B-bf52 burn (14 finding-bearing rounds / 46 review runs) — and worse, it took 12 rounds to discover a task was ill-posed (F-058: CHK-003 was unreachable from the message text; the story ended NOT DELIVERED), while F-059 shows plan.md claimed items delivered from round 4 onward and was never corrected. A numeric cap alone would not surface unreachability; a forced adjudication point would.

Extend, do NOT rebuild: core/review-convergence.ts already has a stall/trend detector (STALL_MIN_ROUNDS=4, STALL_WINDOW=3 non-improving window), but handlers/transition-effects.ts:284-289 consumes it advisory-only inside a try/catch that never blocks the transition — it only appends text. core/convergence-breaker.ts is the only hard brake today, but it counts ADVANCES (maxAdvance=20, AUTO_RECOVERY_BUDGET=1, cleared by story_resume --ack), so 14 review rounds passed under it. This story hardens the stall detector into a blocking decision point at the review-round mint site, adds the structured resolution actions that clear it (including declaring a checklist item unreachable — the F-058 case), and adds a hard ceiling / privileged override that does not double-count with the existing convergence-breaker or story_resume --ack. The optional PreToolUse seatbelt on review_run_start (spec §4) is not part of this story's acceptance criteria and is left to its own follow-on.
